title: Elazar ben Dinai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Mishnah Sotah 9:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Sotah.9.9) preserves his name disparagingly: when murderers multiplied, the broken-necked-heifer ceremony ceased. Elazar ben Dinai, formerly called Techinah ben Perishah, came to be called ben HaRatzchan, son of the murderer. [Ketubot 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.27a.6) also mentions “Ben Donai’s wife.” [Tosafot Yom Tov](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_Yom_Tov_on_Mishnah_Sotah.9.9.3) cites Rabbi Zanvil’s proposed reading, “At first [he was called] ben Perishah.”[^1]

notes.text: The linked Mishnah calls him Eliezer ben Dinai, also known as Techinah ben Perishah, and says that he came to be called ben HaRatzchan. Hyman has Elazar. Tosafot Yom Tov quotes Rabbi Zanvil Katz’s proposal to read “at first” in place of “Techinah” and then rejects that proposal. The cited Ketubot passage mentions Ben Donai’s wife.
The consulted Mishnah Sotah 9:9 writes Eliezer ben Dinai, while Hyman’s notice writes Elazar. The name forms are preserved separately.
